# Muster

Muster is an open source AI agent framework you can self-host and audit. It is
MIT-licensed, written in TypeScript, and stores sessions, memory and the token
ledger locally.

Website: https://themuster.dev/
Repository: https://github.com/Dkm0315/muster
License: MIT

## What makes it different

Most agent harnesses record file changes from what the agent reports it did.
Muster derives them by observing the workspace. It pins a git baseline when a
run starts, re-derives the full change set from git plus the filesystem every
cycle, hashes file content before and after, and emits a deterministic receipt.

Measured live on 2026-08-27 (docs/STRATEGY_V2.md §9), across 5 runs against the
Codex app-server protocol — 3 protocol probes and 2 head-to-head recordings:

- Codex `item/fileChange/patchUpdated`: 0 of 5 real edits reported
- Codex `turn/diff/updated`: 0 in both head-to-head runs
- Muster observer `workspace.patch`: reported the edit in both runs it was
  attached to, diff verified by `git apply`
- Detection latency: 86ms (earlier run 75ms) against a 1000ms budget
- Cross-run receipt determinism: two observer processes, different temp dirs,
  ~40 minutes apart, same logical change → byte-identical receiptHash

The finding is version- and model-specific and should be re-measured against
each Codex release rather than assumed permanent.

## Honest limits

- Muster ships 34 capability packs, of which only 2 are substantial.
- It does not compete on plugin breadth. OpenClaw (387.8k stars, 83,433 commits)
  and Hermes Agent (237.1k stars, 25,737 commits) have far deeper ecosystems.
- Grant-based memory sharing (audience, purpose, expiry, revocation) is
  specified but not yet shipped; QM's grant model works today.
- `workspace.patch.diff` would broadcast raw file content unredacted; nothing
  emits it yet, and a redaction layer must land before anything does.
- Muster publishes no star count of its own. It is early.

## Core capabilities

- Observed file-change truth with deterministic, reproducible receipts
- Append-only event spine: 22 typed events, monotonic sequences, fencing tokens,
  idempotency keys, and a reducer invariant rejecting secrets or chain-of-thought
- Scoped memory lanes: tenant, workspace, user, role, session — with leakage tests
- Local token ledger with replay-waste flags; `muster benchmark` measures 875.8k
  naive tokens vs 355.2k (59.4% reduction) across 5 scenarios / 170 turns,
  deterministically and with no model calls
- Eval-gated learning: feedback becomes a test fixture before behaviour changes
- Pluggable runtimes: native, Codex, Claude Code, Cursor SDK, OpenHands, Pi
- MCP capability policy: include/exclude, OAuth setup, result caps, circuit breakers
- Channel gateway: terminal, web, Telegram, Slack, Google Chat, Teams, Discord, WhatsApp
- ERPNext / Frappe context packs: DocTypes, fields, workflows, reports, scripts,
  permission-aware setup — the one integration that is deep rather than declared
- Multi-provider routing that keeps governance outside the model provider
